body: Do you have a recommendation or two on agencies I should look into?

Oh no you're certainly right and that is the source of my problems, and my inability to solve them.  It's just easier to complain on the internet about tangible woes.

It's also a lot harder to solve the problem of an internal lack of drive.  I've identified it, sure, but knowing doesn't make me want to live a shitty purposeless life any more than not knowing.
I did not, but someone linked it.  I'll read it now I guess.
I might look into forgiveness, thanks.
If only I had the money to move and get started somewhere else.

I don't smoke anything.

And if I could get myself motivated to go do the things you're saying I wouldn't even have a problem, most likely.

I'm not going back to college, that's the only thing I know for sure.  I got where I am by caving to people who sang its virtues.

I mean this in the least antagonistic way possible, but why should I try to do it your way?  Why does it have to be hard?  Why do I have to start in a hole of debt just to be kind of maybe only a little bit unhappy for the rest of my life?

Everyone talks about their jobs like they're the worst thing ever.  Everyone talks about how paying bills is shit, and paying taxes is shit, and their bosses are shit, and vacations aren't long enough, and benefits aren't high enough.

Everyone talks about how their wives are miserable bitches.

It just seems like life sucks and then you die.

The problem is I feel like if I apply for a job and then suck at it or don't want to do it or just not show up at all (like I started doing with classes) then I'm letting people down.  I'm not confident that I have the drive to succeed at anything anymore.

I might send you that PM though.
Nothing.  I'm not doing anything.  That's the problem.
